title: More children paid for than the licence allows
question: Where does the money, the funded places or the stated count of children come to more than the operator is licensed to look after at one time?
finding: No public record counts funded children at each centre, so three proxies were tested. 3 of 23 operators hold State contracts for 2025-26 that would pay for more full-time children than they have licensed places even at the City's highest rate ($36,324 a year for an infant), led by Faces SF: $15.6 million, or 428 children against 271 places; 6 more exceed their places at the preschool rate. 0 Head Start comparisons show more funded places than licensed places. In 2019 the City Controller, using enrolment data the public cannot see, found 69 of 579 subsidised providers (12 percent) potentially over capacity.
how: A State contract is a sum of money, not a count of children, so each operator's general child-care and preschool contract maximums for 2025-26 were divided by the City's published full-time rates for January to June 2026 ($36,324 a year for an infant, $25,380 for a preschooler) to give the fewest full-time children the money could pay for, and set against the capacity of all its open San Francisco centre licences added together. Head Start funded places are from the federal locator, by address and by grantee. Stated children are the largest count of children on the organization's latest tax return. Each counts a different thing: a contract maximum is money, a Head Start place is a funded slot, a tax-return figure is children served over a year, and a licensed place is a child present at one moment.
limits: A licensed place is not a child. A part-day programme can serve two children in one place each day: the City's own preschool subsidy pays for sessions of 2.5 to 3.5 hours, and the Controller noted that part-time enrolment can make a provider look over capacity when it is not. A contract may also pay for care that is not delivered in the operator's own licensed centres. State contract figures are maximums, not payments, and the City rate used as a yardstick is the City's highest, so the child counts here are low estimates. The test cannot be run properly without funded places and enrolment per site, which the City and the State hold and do not publish (the City's monthly enrolment reports from its two agencies; the State's monthly attendance reports from contractors).

rows.test: State contracts, turned into full-time children at City rates
rows.unit: full-time children at the infant rate
rows.verdict: More than its places even at the City infant rate
rows.arithmetic: $15.6 million of State general child-care and preschool contracts for 2025-26 divided by the City's full-time infant rate of $36,324 a year is 428 children, and by its preschool rate of $25,380 is 613, against 271 licensed places. Possible explanations: part-day sessions (two children can use one place in a day), care delivered away from the operator's own licensed centres, and a contract maximum that is not fully earned; the allocation tables do not say which.
